analysis.subject: earth-science
analysis.pageCoverage: Covers history of geologic time ideas from Steno stratigraphic laws and Hutton uniformitarianism through Kelvin cooling estimates to radiometric dating and modern Earth age

overview.headline: Deep time from Steno laws to radiometric dating and modern Earth age

keyPoints.point: Modern science places Earth age at 4.54 billion years and reflects deep time thinking
keyPoints.quote: Earth is 4.54 billion years old, a span of time that is hard for many people to grasp.

keyPoints.point: Lord Kelvin cooling magma calculations yielded an age of 20–400 million years
keyPoints.quote: Lord Kelvin’s cooling-magma calculations yielded an age of 20–400 million years.

keyPoints.point: Steno principles of original horizontality and superposition order sedimentary layers by relative time
keyPoints.quote: The law of original horizontality says that sedimentary layers are deposited in horizontal layers.

keyPoints.point: Hutton proposed uniformitarianism that processes seen today shaped Earth in the past and future
keyPoints.quote: In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

keyTerms.gloss: principle that geologic processes operating today also shaped Earth in the past
keyTerms.quote: In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

keyTerms.gloss: branch of geology concerned with study of rock layers
keyTerms.quote: These basic principles of stratigraphy — or the branch of geology concerned with the study of rock layers

keyTerms.gloss: length of time for half of parent isotopes to decay to daughter isotope
keyTerms.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

keyTerms.gloss: pattern where species become extinct and are replaced showing characteristic age
keyTerms.quote: In 1815, Smith developed the law of faunal succession, which states that species become extinct and are replaced by new species

keyTerms.gloss: gaps in geologic record that represent missing time
keyTerms.quote: He also understood the concept of unconformities (gaps in the geologic record that represent missing time)
